html:
Hipparchia of Maroneia was a Cynic philosopher who lived in Athens around 325 BCE. She is one of the very few women philosophers of ancient Greece whose life we know something about.

She was born in Maroneia in Thrace to a wealthy family that moved to Athens. Her brother studied with Crates of Thebes, the leading Cynic of the day. The Cynics, followers of Diogenes, scorned money, comfort and custom and lived simply in public; see Cynicism. Hipparchia fell in love with Crates and said she would kill herself if she could not marry him. Crates is said to have stood up, dropped his cloak and told her that this was all he owned.

She married him anyway and lived with him as an equal, in poverty, on the streets of Athens, dressed like a man and going to dinners and debates. When a philosopher mocked her for leaving the loom, she answered that she had spent her time on education instead. Most of what we know comes from Diogenes Laertius. Crates later taught Zeno, the founder of Stoicism.
sum: Hipparchia of Maroneia was a Cynic philosopher who lived in Athens around 325 BCE. She is one of the very few women philosophers of ancient Greece whose life we know something about.
